Apple___Apple_scab.description: Fungal disease (Venturia inaequalis) causing olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves and scabby lesions on fruit.
prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn
Prune for open canopy and air flow
treatment: Apply protectant fungicide (captan, mancozeb or sulfur) from green tip
Use systemic fungicide (myclobutanil) during wet spring weather

Apple___Black_rot.description: Fungal disease (Botryosphaeria obtusa) producing purple-ringed 'frog-eye' leaf spots, fruit rot and cankers.
prevention: Prune out dead wood and cankers
Keep trees well watered and fertilised to avoid stress
treatment: Cut out cankers during dry weather
Apply captan or thiophanate-methyl fungicide from petal fall

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Fungal disease (Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae) with bright yellow-orange leaf spots; needs juniper/cedar as an alternate host.
prevention: Remove nearby juniper or cedar galls
treatment: Spray myclobutanil or mancozeb from pink bud through petal fall
Remove heavily infected leaves

Apple___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The apple leaf appears healthy.
prevention: Monitor regularly for scab and rust
treatment: No treatment required

Blueberry___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The blueberry leaf appears healthy.
treatment: No treatment required

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: Fungal disease (Podosphaera clandestina) forming white powdery growth on leaves and young shoots, causing curling and reduced vigour.
prevention: Prune for airflow and sunlight penetration
Water at the base, not overhead
treatment: Apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or myclobutanil at first sign
Remove and destroy infected shoots

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The cherry leaf appears healthy.
prevention: Keep orchard floor clean of debris
treatment: No treatment required

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.disease: Cercospora leaf spot Gray leaf spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Fungal disease (Cercospora zeae-maydis) causing long, rectangular, tan-to-grey lesions parallel to leaf veins.
prevention: Till residue under to reduce inoculum
treatment: Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicide at tasseling (VT/R1) if pressure is high

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Fungal disease (Puccinia sorghi) producing small, powdery, cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
prevention: Plant early to avoid cool, humid late-season spread
treatment: Apply foliar fungicide (azoxystrobin, propiconazole) if pustules appear before tasseling on susceptible hybrids

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Fungal disease (Exserohilum turcicum) causing long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions that can destroy leaf area.
treatment: Apply foliar fungicide at early disease onset (VT-R2)
Avoid overhead irrigation late in the day

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The maize leaf appears healthy.
treatment: No treatment required

Grape___Black_rot.description: Fungal disease (Guignardia bidwellii) causing brown circular leaf lesions with dark borders and shrivelled black 'mummy' berries.
prevention: Remove mummified berries and infected canes
Open the canopy through training and pruning
treatment: Apply mancozeb, myclobutanil or captan from early shoot growth until fruit set

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Complex fungal trunk disease causing 'tiger-stripe' interveinal leaf discolouration and spotted berries; can kill vines.
treatment: No fully effective cure: remove and burn affected wood
Trunk surgery on valuable vines; replace severely affected vines

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Fungal leaf spot (Pseudocercospora vitis) with irregular dark brown lesions, leading to early defoliation.
treatment: Apply copper-based or mancozeb fungicide
Remove severely infected leaves

Grape___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The grape leaf appears healthy.
treatment: No treatment required

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Devastating bacterial disease (Candidatus Liberibacter) spread by the Asian citrus psyllid; causes blotchy yellow leaves, lopsided bitter fruit and tree decline.
prevention: Control psyllid vectors with insecticide and biological control
Scout regularly and report suspect trees
treatment: There is no cure: remove and destroy infected trees to protect the grove
Nutritional programmes can prolong productivity of infected trees

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni) causing small angular water-soaked leaf spots that drop out ('shot-hole') and pitted fruit.
prevention: Use windbreaks and avoid excess nitrogen
treatment: Apply copper bactericide in early season
Oxytetracycline sprays where registered

Peach___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The peach leaf appears healthy.
prevention: Clean up fallen fruit and leaves
Monitor for leaf curl and bacterial spot
treatment: No treatment required

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas spp.) causing small, dark, water-soaked leaf spots and raised scabby fruit lesions.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed or transplants
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for 2-3 years
treatment: Apply copper plus mancozeb sprays at first symptoms
Remove and destroy heavily infected plants

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The pepper leaf appears healthy.
treatment: No treatment required

Potato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease (Alternaria solani) with dark brown concentric 'target' rings on older leaves, causing yellowing and defoliation.
prevention: Keep plants well fertilised and irrigated, avoid stress
treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb or azoxystrobin at first symptoms
Remove infected lower leaves

Potato___Late_blight.description: Aggressive oomycete disease (Phytophthora infestans) with water-soaked dark lesions, white mould underside and rapid plant collapse. Cause of the Irish famine.
prevention: Destroy volunteer potatoes and cull piles
treatment: Apply protectant fungicides (chlorothalonil, mancozeb) then systemic (metalaxyl, cymoxanil) in wet weather
Destroy infected haulm before harvest

Potato___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The potato leaf appears healthy.
treatment: No treatment required

Raspberry___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The raspberry leaf appears healthy.
treatment: No treatment required

Soybean___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The soybean leaf appears healthy.
prevention: Rotate with corn or small grains
treatment: No treatment required

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: Fungal disease (Podosphaera xanthii) producing white powdery patches on leaves that reduce photosynthesis and yield.
prevention: Water in the morning at the soil level
treatment: Spray sulfur, neem oil, potassium bicarbonate or a labelled fungicide
Remove heavily infected leaves

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Fungal disease (Diplocarpon earlianum) causing purple blotches that merge and make leaf edges look scorched.
prevention: Renovate beds after harvest and remove old leaves
treatment: Apply captan or myclobutanil fungicide
Remove infected foliage

Strawberry___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The strawberry leaf appears healthy.
prevention: Use raised beds with good drainage
treatment: No treatment required

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas spp.) causing small dark greasy spots on leaves and rough scabby fruit spots.
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation and handling wet plants
treatment: Apply copper-based bactericide with mancozeb
Remove and destroy infected plants late in the season

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease (Alternaria solani) with brown concentric 'bull's-eye' spots on older leaves and stem lesions.
prevention: Stake and prune to improve airflow
treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb or copper fungicide every 7-10 days
Maintain plant nutrition

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Oomycete disease (Phytophthora infestans) causing large greasy grey-green lesions and white mould in humid weather; can destroy a crop in days.
prevention: Avoid wet foliage; water early in the day
treatment: Apply preventive chlorothalonil or copper fungicide; use systemic products after infection
Remove and bag (do not compost) infected plants

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Fungal disease (Passalora fulva) with pale yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces and olive-brown mould underneath, common in humid greenhouses.
treatment: Apply chlorothalonil or copper fungicide
Remove infected leaves

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Fungal disease (Septoria lycopersici) with many small circular spots with dark borders and grey centres, starting on lower leaves.
treatment: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb at first symptoms
Remove infected lower leaves

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Pest damage by two-spotted spider mites (Tetranychus urticae): fine stippling, bronzing and webbing on leaves in hot, dry conditions.
prevention: Keep plants well watered to reduce stress
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural enemies
treatment: Spray with water to dislodge mites
Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil or a miticide (abamectin)

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Fungal disease (Corynespora cassiicola) with brown spots with concentric rings and yellow halos on leaves and fruit.
prevention: Improve airflow through staking and pruning
treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, azoxystrobin or mancozeb
Remove infected leaves

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Viral disease (TYLCV) transmitted by whiteflies; leaves curl upward and turn yellow, plants are stunted with poor fruit set.
prevention: Control whiteflies (yellow sticky traps, insect nets)
Remove weeds and infected plants promptly
treatment: No cure for infected plants: rogue and destroy them
Use insecticides or neem oil to reduce whitefly spread

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Viral disease (ToMV) causing mottled light/dark green mosaic and distorted, fern-like leaves; spreads mechanically and on seed.
prevention: Use virus-free seed and resistant varieties
Do not smoke or handle tobacco before touching plants
treatment: No cure: remove and destroy infected plants
Disinfect stakes, tools and greenhouse surfaces

Tomato___healthy.description: No disease symptoms detected. The tomato leaf appears healthy.
prevention: Mulch and water at the base
Scout weekly for early signs of disease
treatment: No treatment required
